notes:
Account summary
- Kiteframe is a mid-market SaaS platform selling customer support automation + knowledge base search to ~1k downstream tenants.
- They currently split spend across multiple LLM providers and are getting pressure from Finance to implement per-feature (per route) chargeback.
- Primary buyer: Eng Platform + FinOps; Security is pulled in early due to their enterprise customers.

What they want from Redwood
- Strong requirement: route-level cost attribution that can be exported (CSV + JSON) and used in their FinOps workflow.
  - Quote (from demo): "If we can’t export route spend weekly, it won’t get adopted internally." (FinOps lead)
- Need quick answers in console:
  - "Which endpoints are costing us the most?"
  - "Which models are driving spend on those endpoints?"
  - "What changed week-over-week?" (they do weekly cost reviews)

Use cases / workload
- Routes they called out:
  - /v1/support/auto-reply (chat; latency sensitive)
  - /v1/support/summarize (batchy; cost sensitive)
  - /v1/kb/search (embeddings + rerank; throughput sensitive)
- Traffic: spiky weekdays; bulk backfills happen monthly (need safeguards so exports don’t time out).
- Wants model fallback behavior but needs reporting that still ties spend to the original product route.

Evaluation scope (proposed)
- Start with Hosted API in staging; likely land on Dedicated (for predictable throughput + data isolation) if the numbers work.
- Tag 8–12 routes via SDK/header; keep route naming stable (no tenant/user IDs).
- Validate:
  - Top routes view: spend ranking + quick filters (time range, env, region).
  - Route detail: model breakdown + deltas vs prior period.
  - Export: CSV + JSON schema is usable by Finance; bounded size/time range; audit log evidence for export/download.

Key requirements / questions
- Route tagging
  - They can adopt an explicit route header in their gateway, but asked for SDK support too.
  - Concern: internal services currently use dynamic names (workspace IDs). They asked for guidance on normalization/guardrails.
- Export/reporting
  - Needs: report includes route, model, input/output tokens, cached tokens, total cost, latency p50/p95, and error rate.
  - Asked whether they can schedule exports. Answer: not in initial GA; workaround is manual export + API/job endpoint if available during beta.
  - Asked about schema stability: they want versioning/forward-compat guidance.
- Reconciliation
  - They will compare exports to invoice totals; ok with small deltas if explained (late-arriving metering events, retention windows, rounding).
- Security/compliance
  - Must-have: SSO/SAML, RBAC scoped to org/project, export audit logging (who/when/filters), retention controls.
  - Data residency: prefers US; open to EU later for a subset of tenants.
  - VPC deployment preference for production; asked if audit logs are available in Private as well.

Risks / red flags
- Route-cardinality: if they don’t clean up naming, they will blow up dimensions and end up with lots of "Other/Hashed" buckets (we need to set expectations + provide naming conventions).
- Export performance: they initially asked for 90-day exports; we should steer to bounded time ranges and/or pagination.

Internal plan / who’s involved
- Owner (AE): Ava Chen
- SE: Alex Martinez
- Product context referenced: in-console usage insights (cost drivers by route) + export/audit logging workstream.

Next steps (agreed)
1) Kiteframe to implement route tagging for top routes (no tenant IDs; follow Redwood naming conventions).
2) Redwood to share:
   - Export CSV schema + limits (rows/time range) and audit event field list.
   - Guidance on route normalization + cardinality guardrails.
3) Schedule evaluation check-in after 1 week of staging traffic replay; review top routes + exported report with FinOps.

Open questions
- How we attribute cost when smart routing falls back mid-request (they want both: requested model vs served model; at minimum, route stays stable).
- Whether Dedicated in a VPC can meet their SSO + audit evidence requirements without extra work.
